change_reason: initial filing after round-2 kill-pair adjudication

severity.label: low
severity.rationale: The only network-wide double-spend protection for private payments (the spend-proof uniqueness check) keys its conflict match on the unit's claimed author address rather than the output owner the proof commits to. A sender who retains the bearer spend proof can place a second 'good' unit carrying the same proof under a different address with no conflict detection and no resolution. Impact is bounded: the payload-side binding rejects the ghost's payload (no direct theft of the double-spent value), and the victim's unit is not voided in the same-branch case; merchant exposure is conditional on acceptance flows keyed on unit inclusion. The durable effect is ledger-integrity degradation (permanent unresolved duplicate-spend records) and a payment-race vector. Low with a Medium ceiling conditional on merchant acceptance flows.

claims.attacker_model: a private-payment SENDER who retains the spend proof P (bearer secret: blinding generated by the sender, stored in the sender's outputs row and private payload)
preconditions: sender has sent a private payment creating output X for the recipient (holds P)
the recipient has spent X (or will) — a row (P, recipient_address) exists

mechanism.statement: validateSpendProofs (validation.js:1637-1654) builds the conflict query keyed on (spend_proof, claimed-address) where the claimed address is the unit's own author (validation.js:1557-1568), never the output owner. The spend proof P cryptographically commits to the output owner (inputs.js:73-80). A unit authored by the sender carrying the same P is checked under (P, sender) — the victim's row (P, recipient) never matches — so the re-spend is accepted as 'good' by every node with no conflict detection. For private payments this check is the ONLY network-wide double-spend protection: the input-level check (checkInputDoubleSpend) requires the private payload, which is not in the unit (bPrivate is set only in the payload flow, validation.js:2695), so it cannot run network-wide.

reachability.statement: Empirically demonstrated: the victim's spend is saved with its (P, victim) row; the attacker's re-spend with the same P under the attacker's address is accepted and saved as 'good' (IR-F3 independent run + DB read: two rows with the identical spend proof; r1 exp A_own). Order-independent and network-wide (unit-level check identical on every node).
causal_spine: sender retains blinding and recomputes P for the recipient's output X
sender authors unit A carrying spend_proofs [{address: sender, spend_proof: P}]
unit-level check queries (P, sender) — no row matches
A is accepted as 'good' by every node
two 'good' units carry the same spend proof; no resolution mechanism fires (fork machinery is author-keyed)

impact_claims: c-003-impact: private-payment double-spend protection defeated at the network level; permanent unresolved duplicate-spend records on the MC path

c-004-impact: payment-race vector — the sender can silently contest a merchant's included payment (public model emits a clean rejection; private model emits nothing); merchant exposure conditional on acceptance flows keyed on inclusion
c-005-impact-bounds: no direct theft demonstrated (the ghost's payload is rejected by the payload-side owner binding, divisible_asset.js:159); the victim's unit is not voided in the same-branch case
claims.uncertainty: Fork-variant win probability (MC race) not demonstrated; merchant-exposure escalation conditional on external acceptance flows. Whether Obyte's private-payment merchants use inclusion-based acceptance is outside the core library.
claims.conflicting_evidence: The kill side argued the bearer model is by-design and the fork race is the standard resolution; the establish side demonstrated the input-level check cannot run network-wide for private payloads and the fork machinery never resolves the same-branch case (two 'good' units persist). Both are incorporated: the design may intend the sender's retention, but the check's keying is not explained by it.

fresh_state_properties: independent DB read of spend_proofs and units tables in the reviewer run

contamination_disposition.note: The property is a pure function of the check's keying; deterministic across runs; verified by two independent runs (r1, IR-F3)

claim_proofs.note: Two independent runs saved both units and read the DB: spend_proofs holds (P, victim) from the victim's spend and (P, attacker) from the attacker's re-spend; the units table shows both 'good'

control_applicability.note: same P + same address -> clean rejection 'conflicting spend proof in inner unit' (the check works within an address); same P + different address -> silently accepted
no independent positive oracle; the contrast control is the evidence

adjudication.justification: Kill-pair adjudication (orchestrator): establish side demonstrated the check is the only network-wide protection and is keyed out of reach; kill side demonstrated the impact ceiling (no direct theft, payload binding, no voiding). IR-F3 independently confirmed the empirical property. Verdict: real defect, Low — the uniqueness key should bind the output owner; Medium ceiling conditional on merchant acceptance flows.
